landing.title: Cold-chain compliance AI for the Gulf
landing.subtitle: Automate inspection of temperature logs, QC forms, chat messages, and voice notes. Grounded in GCC food-safety law. Every training label from a deterministic rules engine, never from an LLM.
landing.valueTitle: Business value for regulators and operators
landing.value1Body: Maps to Gulf Standardization Organization food-safety frameworks and jurisdiction-specific instruments (SFDA, ESMA, MoPH Qatar, and more).
landing.value2Body: Every record carries wave, cell, rules-engine hash, and screener verdict. Built for HACCP cold-chain audits and traceability.
landing.value3Body: Gate A/B KPIs score corpus quality before training spend. Rescore existing data in one command without regenerating.
landing.value4Body: English and Arabic artifacts with authenticity scoring. Designed for how GCC logistics teams actually communicate.
landing.jurisdictions: SA | AE | QA | BH | KW | OM
landing.seoTitle: GCC Cold-Chain Compliance AI | GSO Food Safety
landing.seoDesc: AI-assisted cold-chain compliance for GCC food operators. GSO-aligned, rules-engine labels, Gate A/B quality gates.

simulation.seoDesc: Interactive demo: synthesize temperature logs, run the rules engine, and preview field artifacts.
simulation.title: How it works - live simulation
simulation.subtitle: Pick a product, fault scenario, and jurisdiction. The rules engine labels the shipment before any LLM sees the data, exactly like the production pipeline.
simulation.empty: Configure inputs and run to see temperature physics, disposition, and pipeline steps.
simulation.explainWhat: This is a sandbox that walks through one synthetic shipment record end to end, exactly the way the automated pipeline would: it builds a temperature history, applies the deterministic rules engine (never an AI guess) to decide accept / hold-for-QA / reject, and previews what a field report about it might look like.
simulation.explainInput: Choose a product, a fault scenario (e.g. door left open, compressor failure, sensor drift), a jurisdiction, an artifact format, and a random seed — these control what kind of shipment gets generated.
simulation.explainOutput: The generated temperature readings on a chart, the rules-engine disposition and which rule decided it, the excursion time and remaining shelf life, a preview artifact, and any guardrail issues found in that preview text.

ask.title: Ask the Compliance Engine
ask.subtitle: Ask a free-form question about a cold-chain edge case. Every answer is grounded only in this repo's own guardrail pack and law citations — the model is told to say so, not guess, when something you ask about isn't in the pack.
ask.seoDesc: Ask free-form cold-chain compliance questions, grounded in the GCC guardrail pack and law citations, reasoned through a 4-step chain.
ask.placeholder: e.g. Data logger shows -15°C for 30 mins during a defrost cycle, but the GSO clause allows variance for 'unavoidable technical operations'. Is this a violation?
ask.notConfigured: K2 is not configured on this deployment (K2_API_KEY unset in .env).
ask.disclaimer: Decision support only, not legal advice — a licensed QA/compliance authority makes the final call.
ask.citationsVerified: All citations verified against the guardrail pack
ask.citationsUnverified: unverified citation(s) — not found in the retrieved guardrail pack
ask.empty: Ask a question above to start.
ask.productMismatchSuffix: — your question matched this better than the selected product
ask.unverifiedWarning: Citation check flagged unverified references — confirm against the source pack before acting on this answer.
ask.explainWhat: This is a compliance question-and-answer assistant. Describe a real situation you're reviewing — a temperature log, a claimed exemption, a borderline reading — and it reasons through it in four visible steps, citing only the rules and GSO clauses actually on file, and telling you plainly when something you mentioned isn't in that file.
ask.explainInput: Pick the jurisdiction and product if you know them (the assistant will also try to work them out from your wording), then type your question in plain English or Arabic — e.g. "Data logger shows -15°C for 30 minutes during a defrost cycle, but the driver says GSO allows an exemption for unavoidable technical operations. Is this a violation?"
ask.explainOutput: A step-by-step reasoning trace (which law/rules apply, what the numbers mean, what-if scenarios, then a final recommendation) plus a citation check flagging any rule ID or GSO clause the answer mentioned that isn't actually in the loaded rule pack — so you know what to double-check before acting on it.

liveops.title: LiveOps
liveops.subtitle: Generate a random truck scenario and watch it reasoned through in real time, from raw telemetry to a GSO-aligned recommendation.
liveops.explainWhat: This simulates a live truck event: a random, physically plausible shipment situation is generated the same deterministic way the rest of this system works, then narrated by the assistant in three steps so you can see how a live alert would actually be reasoned through, end to end.
liveops.explainInput: Press "New Scenario" to generate a random truck situation (product, jurisdiction, fault type, and telemetry are all randomized). Optionally add a free-text note the way a driver or site officer might phone one in, then press "Narrate".
liveops.explainOutput: What happened on the truck in plain language, why it is or isn't a compliance problem with the specific GSO clause or rule involved, and a GSO-aligned recommendation for what to do next — plus the same citation check used on the Ask page, and a one-click branded PDF of the whole decision trace.
liveops.scenarioHint: A new random scenario uses the same rules engine as the Simulation page — nothing about the disposition is guessed by the AI.
liveops.officerNotePlaceholder: e.g. Driver says the door was opened briefly for a routine inspection at the border crossing.
